The **GLM Solution: Link Function**

- Link (g): Map Outcome → Predictors
    - without breaking the boundary rules
- Inverse Link (g^-1): Map Predictors → Outcome
    - Turn a mathematical score into real-world predictions

| Model | Random Component (y) | Bounded Expected Values | Link Function | Inverse Link |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Logistic | Binomial (1/0) | Probability PE(0,1) | Logit Link: ln(p/1-p) | g^-1 Sigmoid Function |
| Poisson | Poisson | E(0,inf) | Log Link: log(μ) | e^n/1+e^n e^n |

The **Recidivism** Algorithim

- Likelihood to commit a crime again
- Phrenology: outdated personality traits based on physical attributes
- crime^n = prison time
    - n=number of offenses

## Geographic CV + Logistic Regression I

- Random k-folds doesn’t factor spatial location on train vs test data
    - Spatial leakage
- **District folds**, leaves one district out
    - Geographically segmented training and testing data sets instead of a random split
    - More comparative, x district predict better/worse than other districts

## probability

- odds = p/(1-p)
    - How many more times likely is it to happen than it doesn’t?
- p = 0.8, odds?
    - odds = 0.8/1-0.8 = 4
- p = 0.455 → 0.455/1-0.455 = o = 0.835
- For every 100 people not rearrested, 84 are.
- prob: 0 to 1
- odss: 0 to inf
- log odds: -inf to +inf
- negative binomial: logit models log(odds)
- poisson: log(expected count)
- **log** **odds** of a **linear** model to get a **binomial** outcome
- sigmoid. log odd
- predict(model_fit, type= “link”) log odds default output
- predict(model_fit, type= “response”) probability output

## confusion matrix

predicted + actual = true positive (**TP**)

predicted + did not = false positive (**FP**)

did not predict + actual = false negative (**FN**)

did not predict + did not = true negative (**TN**)

- **Sensitivity** = TP/(TP+FN) → of all people who had disease, how many did we catch
- **Specificity** = TN/(TN+FP) → of all people who didn’t have it, how many did we correctly leave alone?
- **Precision** = TP/(TP+FP) → of all predicted sick, how many actually were?
